items.title: From mocked to mainstream: how Spain’s far-right Vox transformed its fortunes
items.raw:
Party that won just 0.2% of the vote in 2016 is on course for almost 20% this time and could be part of next government
Almost exactly eight years ago, a video clip of a stocky, bearded man riding a horse through western Andalucía went viral in Spain. The rider was Santiago Abascal, the leader of the far-right Vox party, the soundtrack was a bombastic snatch of the Lord of the Rings score, and the caption was an equally unsubtle callback to the 700-year fight to wrest the Iberian peninsula from Islamic rule. “La Reconquista comenzará en tierras andaluzas,” it read – the reconquest will begin on Andalucían soil.
Celebrated by some, jeered by others – and inventively lampooned by those with sufficient skill and time on their hands – the video didn’t seem quite as amusing three weeks later when Vox broke through into the political mainstream by winning 12 seats in Andalucía’s regional parliament.

items.title: Monday briefing: What could Andy Burnham’s reset mean for the UK?
items.raw:
In today’s newsletter: The prime minister has reopened the debate over a future relationship with a changed EU – as the bloc faces the rise of the far right, a protectionist economic agenda and growing defence ambitions
Good morning. Nobody really wants to think about Brexit any more, save for the original Brexiters, who seem delighted that Andy Burnham’s “reset” with the EU has given them an excuse to get the old gang back together. But arguments about whether the UK should rejoin the EU will reignite in parliament this week, as Burnham briefs MPs on the deal he agreed on Friday.
That deal wasn’t so much a victory as the culmination of Keir Starmer’s incrementalist approach to UK-EU relations. Its core agreements haven’t been ratified by member states yet, and the EU won’t sign them off until Britain resolves a dispute over tuition fees for European students. Burnham is apparently “determined” to take the UK back into the EU, but don’t expect any progress on that before the next general election.

The warning came as the UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons concluded without an agreement on an instrument for regulating autonomous weapons.

items.title: ‘The show is starting soon. Please turn on your headphones.’
items.raw:
Love Me uses Auracast broadcasts both for accessibility and the sound design. | Photo: Curtis Brown	

Up a few concrete steps and through the front door of a 200-year-old row house in New York City, I follow a crowd of people into the 178-seat SoHo Playhouse. As we filter to our seats, ushers hand each person a black drawstring bag with a pair of wired headphones connected to a small Auracast receiver. Then, soon after the play begins, we're instructed to put them on.

items.title: Nintendo’s Switch 2 console is $50 off for Black Friday
items.raw:
Those hoping to save some cash on a Nintendo Switch 2 can do so starting today, November 22nd, through Saturday, December 5th, giving you plenty of time to think about it after Cyber Monday has passed. For a limited time, Nintendo has knocked $50 off one of its two current console bundles, temporarily rolling back the $50 price increase that went into effect in early September.
It’s tough to predict which bundle will be most popular for your household. The Mario Kart World bundle runs $499.99 (previously $549.99) and includes the console, a digital copy of the aforementioned game, and three months of Nintendo Switch Online. Then there’s the Nintendo Switch Sports Resort bundle for $529.99 (price unchanged for Black Friday), which includes the more recent minigame-filled title instead. Both are currently available from Amazon, Best Buy, Walmart, and Nintendo.

 $549.99 $499.99 at Amazon

items.title: California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state
items.raw:
Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded
Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.
Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.
